Alright, I've just finished a series of functional updates to the TUI: added a stream buffer ref, throttled the UI updates in the ticker effect, introduced a queue for mid‑run inputs, and made the submit callback respect the running state. Those changes should improve performance and make input handling more robust.

Now I need to address the UI layout itself. Right now the `<Input>` component is conditionally rendered only when `!running && !approval && !effortMenu`. That means when a turn starts, the input component is unmounted and then remounted after the turn finishes. Unmounting the input causes the Ink layout to recompute, which leads to a noticeable flicker, especially when the terminal is narrow. Also, because the input is destroyed, any internal state (like the cursor position) is lost, which feels jarring to the user.

The goal is to keep the input bar mounted at the bottom of the screen at all times, but disable its interactivity when we’re in a modal state (approval or effort menu). Ink's `<Input>` already has an `active` prop for this purpose, so I can set `active={!approval && !effortMenu}` and let the component stay in the tree. While a turn is running, the input should still accept keystrokes (so the queueing logic works), but the UI should indicate that it's not the primary focus—perhaps by changing the border color to a darker shade when `running` is true.

While I'm here, I also notice the thoughts display: currently it renders the full `thoughtLines` array, which can grow large over a long session. Rendering hundreds of `<Text>` elements each frame is wasteful and can degrade performance. I can trim the displayed thoughts to the most recent 12 lines and also truncate each line to 200 characters, which should be sufficient for readability while keeping the render cheap. The collapsed view already shows only the last thought slice, so this change aligns with that behavior.

Next, the suggestions list is also rendered conditionally inside the same block as the input. Since the input will now always be present, I need to move the suggestions rendering out of the old block and make it appear only when we’re not `running` (so suggestions don’t pop up mid‑turn). I’ll keep the same layout but wrap it in a condition `suggestions.length > 0 && !running`.

Additionally, the box that wraps the input currently uses `borderColor={theme.faint}`. To give a visual cue that the UI is busy, I’ll switch the border color to a darker hue (`"#3A3A3C"`) when `running` is true, otherwise fall back to `theme.faint`. This matches the existing theme palette.

I also need to adjust the surrounding JSX ordering: the thoughts box, approval, effort menu, todos, and spinner should stay where they are, but the input block should be moved down after those, inside a persistent `<Box flexDirection="column">`. That way the input stays at the bottom, and the layout won’t shift when the spinner appears or disappears.

Finally, I have to make sure I preserve all existing props on `<Input>` (onSubmit, onChange, history, suggestionsCount, suggestion handlers, etc.) and add the new `active` prop. I’ll also keep the suggestion accept/complete handlers unchanged.

All these changes map to a single edit of `src/tui.tsx`.
